proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(e_{g,t}=\bar Y_{g,t}-\mathbb E\bar Y_{g,t}\).  By the Gaussian-cell assumption, the variables \(e_{g,t}\), indexed by \(g\in I\) and \(t\in\{0\}\cup I\), are mutually independent, centered Gaussian variables with
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(e_{g,t})=\frac{\sigma ^2}{Nq_g}.
\]
The range assumptions imply \(T-m\ge1\), and for every \(t\le T-m<T\), \(q_{>t}>0\), so every division in the pooled-control definition is valid.  Parallel trends, the effect-surface definition, and the fact that every member of \(C_t\) is untreated at date \(t\) give, for \((g,t)\in O\),
\[
 \mathbb E Z_{g,t}
 =\{\mu^0_{g,t}-\mu^0_{g,0}+\tau_{g,t}\}
  -\frac1{q_{>t}}\sum_{a\in C_t}q_a
       \{\mu^0_{a,t}-\mu^0_{a,0}\}
 =\tau_{g,t}=f_t+u_{g,t}=(Kx)_{g,t}.
\]
The centered score has the exact decomposition
\[
 Z_{g,t}-\mathbb EZ_{g,t}
 =e_{g,t}-\frac1{q_{>t}}\sum_{a\in C_t}q_ae_{a,t}
   +\sum_{a=1}^Tb_{(g,t),a}e_{a,0}.
\]
Independence across dates shows that the covariance of the first two terms in two rows is zero unless \(t=s\).  When \(t=s\), the treated cells \(g,h\in G_t\) are disjoint from the control cells in \(C_t\), and hence that covariance is
\[
 \frac{\sigma^2}{N}\mathbf 1\{t=s\}
 \left(\frac{\mathbf 1\{g=h\}}{q_g}
       +\frac{1}{q_{>t}^2}\sum_{a\in C_t}q_a\right)
 =\frac{\sigma^2}{N}\mathbf 1\{t=s\}
 \left(\frac{\mathbf 1\{g=h\}}{q_g}+\frac1{q_{>t}}\right).
\]
The baseline terms have covariance
\[
 \frac{\sigma^2}{N}\sum_{a=1}^T
       \frac{b_{(g,t),a}b_{(h,s),a}}{q_a}.
\]
Thus the displayed covariance is exactly \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\).  Since \(Z\) is a linear transformation of the jointly Gaussian cell array, it follows that \(Z\sim\mathcal N(Kx,\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}})\).  Finally, \(V\) is positive definite because each of its date blocks contains the positive diagonal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(1/q_g:g\in G_t)\); consequently \(V+b\operatorname{diag}(q)^{-1}b'\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\) are positive definite.

Write \(\mathcal H=\mathcal M_{T,m}-\mathcal M_{T,m}=2\mathcal M_{T,m}\), where the equality follows from convexity and centrosymmetry.  The set \(\mathcal H\) is closed and convex.  For fixed \(r>0\), its intersection with \(\{h:\|Kh\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}\le r\}\) is effectively compact.  Indeed, the coordinates of the deviation component are bounded by \(2B\), all differences of calendar coordinates are bounded by \(2L\), and \(O\ne\varnothing\).  A bound on \(Kh\), together with the deviation bound at any row in \(O\), therefore bounds one calendar coordinate and hence all calendar coordinates.  Coordinates occurring in neither \(K\), \(\ell\), nor a centering equation may be set to zero.  The remaining set is a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.  The maximum defining \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\) is consequently attained.

Monotonicity is immediate from nesting of the norm balls.  If \(h_i\) is feasible at radius \(r_i\), then convexity of \(\mathcal H\) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|K\{\lambda h_1+(1-\lambda)h_2\}\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}
 \le \lambda r_1+(1-\lambda)r_2.
\]
Linearity of \(\ell\) and passage to suprema prove concavity.  Finiteness follows from compactness.

The graph of the argmax correspondence is closed: if \(r_i\to r\) and maximizing \(h_i\to h\), feasibility passes to the limit, while continuity and concavity imply \(\ell(h)=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\).  On each compact radius interval, first minimize \(\|h\|_2\) over this graph and then successively minimize each coordinate over the surviving compact graph.  At each step the inverse image of \((-\infty,a)\) is a countable union of projections of compact sets obtained by restricting the radius to a compact interval and the objective to a rational margin.  It is Borel.  After finitely many coordinates the survivor is a singleton, proving that \(r\mapsto h_r\) is Borel.

Let \(p_r=\partial_+\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\).  The secant-slope inequalities for a finite concave function give
\[
 \omega(s)\le\omega(r)+p_r(s-r)\qquad(s>0),
\]
so \(p_r\) is a supergradient; it is decreasing and right-continuous and hence Borel.  Let \(d\) have calendar component identically one and deviation component zero.  Then \(ad\in\mathcal H\) for every \(a\in\mathbb R\), \(\ell(d)=1\), and \(Kd\ne0\).  Thus \(\omega(r)\) is unbounded as \(r\to\infty\).  Since it is increasing and concave, its right derivative cannot vanish at a finite radius.  A maximizer cannot have a slack norm constraint, because adding a sufficiently small positive multiple of \(d\) would preserve feasibility and strictly increase \(\ell\).  Hence \(p_r>0\) and \(\|Kh_r\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}=r\) for every \(r>0\), so \(\mathcal R_+=(0,\infty)\).

The supporting-hyperplane condition at \(h_r\) is
\[
 \ell(h)-\frac{p_r}{r}\langle Kh_r,Kh\rangle_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}
 \le\omega(r)-rp_r\qquad(h\in\mathcal H).
\]
Indeed, perturb \(h_r\) toward \(h\), apply the supergradient inequality, divide by the perturbation size, and use the directional derivative
\(r^{-1}\langle Kh_r,Kh-Kh_r\rangle_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}\) of the norm.  Applying the result to \(-h\) gives the corresponding absolute bound.

The exact Gaussian law now gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_x(\widehat\theta_r)
 =\left(\frac{p_r}{r}\right)^2\|Kh_r\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}^2
 =p_r^2=s_r^2.
\]
Since \(\mathcal H=2\mathcal M_{T,m}\), the support identity gives
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}|\mathbb E_x\widehat\theta_r-\ell(x)|
 =\frac{\omega(r)-rp_r}{2}=b_r.
\]
Thus the exact maximal squared-error risk is \(b_r^2+s_r^2\).

Both infima in the definition are finite because \(r=1\) is admissible.  They are strictly positive: two distinct common-shift parameters \(\pm ad/2\), for fixed sufficiently small \(a>0\), induce equivalent, nonidentical Gaussian laws, so neither zero maximal squared-error risk nor a zero-length interval having coverage above one half at both points is possible.  Infimum-approaching radii with the stated multiplicative factors therefore exist.  Taking the least admissible radius in a fixed enumeration of rational intervals meeting each sublevel set makes the sequences deterministic.  All displayed procedures are Borel compositions of the selections already established.

Assume \(q_g=1/T\) and \(B=0\).  At \(t=T-r\),
\[
 b_{(g,t),\cdot}=-e_g+\frac1r\mathbf1_{C_t},
\]
and hence, for \(g,h\in G_t\),
\[
 b_{(g,t),\cdot}\operatorname{diag}(q)^{-1}b_{(h,t),\cdot}'
 =T\{\mathbf1(g=h)+1/r\}.
\]
The contemporaneous block has the same entries.  The matched block therefore has diagonal \(2\sigma^2T(1+1/r)/N\) and off-diagonal \(2\sigma^2T/(Nr)\).  A matrix \(aI_p+c\mathbf1\mathbf1'\) has effective common-mean variance \(a/p+c\).  Taking \(p=T-r\), \(a=2\sigma^2T/N\), and \(c=2\sigma^2T/(Nr)\) gives
\[
 v_{T-r}^{\mathrm{diag}}
 =\frac{2\sigma^2T}{N(T-r)}+\frac{2\sigma^2T}{Nr}
 =\frac{2\sigma^2T^2}{Nr(T-r)}.
\]
The definition of \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) makes different date blocks independent, so the generalized least-squares aggregates are independent normals with means \(f_{T-r}\).

Consequently
\[
 S_{m,k}^{\mathrm{diag}}
 =\frac{N}{2\sigma^2T^2}\sum_{r=m}^{m+k-1}r(T-r).
\]
Substitution of \(\sum_{r=m}^{m+k-1}r=k(2m+k-1)/2\) and the difference of the two sums of squares gives exactly the finite expression in the definition.  If \(m=o(k)\) and \(k=o(T)\), then
\[
 \sum_{r=m}^{m+k-1}r(T-r)\sim T\frac{k^2}{2},
 \qquad S_{m,k}^{\mathrm{diag}}\sim\frac{Nk^2}{4\sigma^2T},
\]
so the inverse-information standard error is \(2\sigma\sqrt{T/N}/k\).

The inverse-information weighted average over these dates has bias at most \(L\{(m+k-1)/T\}^\beta\).  For the converse, take opposite Holder paths whose difference at reverse date \(r\) is
\[
 h_{T-r}=\left[d-2L(r/T)^\beta\right]_+,
\]
with \(u=0\).  The inequality \(|r^\beta-s^\beta|\le|r-s|^\beta\) puts the half-paths in the class.  Their squared standardized mean separation is \(\sum_rh_{T-r}^2/v_{T-r}^{\mathrm{diag}}\).  Choosing \(d\) as a sufficiently small constant times the Holder bias plus inverse square-root information makes this separation at most one.  The two-normal testing reduction then gives the matching root-risk lower bound.  Balancing the two terms under \(m=o(k_0)\) yields
\[
 k_0=\left\{\frac{\sigma^2T^{2\beta+1}}{NL^2}\right\}^{1/(2\beta+2)},\qquad
 L(k_0/T)^\beta
 =L^{1/(\beta+1)}\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{NT}\right)^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}.
\]

For \(T=3\) and \(m=1\), order the rows as \((1,1),(1,2),(2,2)\).  In units of \(\sigma^2/N\),
\[
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}=\begin{pmatrix}9&9/2&0\\9/2&12&6\\0&6&12\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}=\begin{pmatrix}9&0&0\\0&12&6\\0&6&12\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For a constant mean, the best linear unbiased variance is \((\mathbf1'\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1)^{-1}\).  Direct inversion gives
\[
 \mathbf1'\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}\mathbf1=\frac7{36},
 \qquad \mathbf1'\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}^{-1}\mathbf1=\frac29,
\]
with normalized weights \((4/7,0,3/7)\) and \((1/2,1/4,1/4)\).  Restoring the common factor proves the variances \(36\sigma^2/(7N)\) and \(9\sigma^2/(2N)\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The dimension-free upper modulus inequality, equivalently the covariance-whitened dual transport certificate, is not closed.
open_obligations.obstruction: The explicit boundary bump supplies the lower direction, but the pooled-date dual has shared-baseline energy of the wrong order. A valid proof needs coefficients that simultaneously control Holder leverage, bounded-deviation leverage, and the full baseline Gram energy.
open_obligations.attempted: I derived the exact coefficient energy identity, constructed the centered positive-part lower lift, and tried pooled inverse-variance and backward baseline-cancellation weights. The former has baseline energy of order T divided by k; the latter does not yet retain the required bounded-deviation sensitivity.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For \(h=(F,U)\in2\mathcal M_{T,m}\), let \(r=T-t\), \(Q_r=\sum_{g\le T-r}q_g\), and \(R_r=1-Q_r\).  Balanced cohorts give \(R_r/Q_r\asymp r/(T-r)\) uniformly for \(r\le\delta T\).  The lower lift can be constructed explicitly: for \(d\ge0\), set
\[
 F_{T-r}=[d-2L(r/T)^\beta]_+,\qquad
 c_r=\min\{F_{T-r},2B,2BR_r/Q_r\},
\]
and put \(U_{g,T-r}=-c_r\) for \(g\le T-r\) and \(U_{g,T-r}=c_rQ_r/R_r\) otherwise.  Then \(\sum_gq_gU_{g,t}=0\), \(|U_{g,t}|\le2B\), and the two endpoints \(\pm(F,U)/2\) are in the model class.  Moreover \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\succeq(\sigma^2/N)V\), while block inversion gives \(\mathbf1'V_t^{-1}\mathbf1=Q_rR_r\).  Hence
\[
 \|K(F,U)\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}^2
 \le\frac N{\sigma^2}\sum_{r=m}^{T-1}Q_rR_r(F_{T-r}-c_r)^2.
\]
This proves a dimension-free lower lift once the positive-part sum is bounded at the optimizing depth.  The missing converse is a dimension-free dual coefficient array \(a\) satisfying simultaneously
\[
 \sum_tA_t=1,\quad
 \sum_t|A_t|\{(T-t)/T\}^{\beta}\lesssim(k/T)^\beta,\quad
 \sum_t\inf_c\sum_g|a_{g,t}\mathbf1\{g\in G_t\}-cq_g|\lesssim k/(T-k),
\]
and
\[
 \sum_t\left\{\sum_{g\in G_t}a_{g,t}^2/q_g+A_t^2/q_{>t}\right\}
 +\sum_j\left\{\sum_{(g,t)\in O}a_{g,t}b_{(g,t),j}\right\}^2/q_j
 \lesssim T/k^2.
\]
These four inequalities would imply the asserted modulus upper bound by Cauchy--Schwarz.  The frozen transport handle does not specify coefficients, and the straightforward pooled-date coefficients have baseline energy of order \(T/k\), not \(T/k^2\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The replacement of the exact covariance modulus by the proposed phase envelope is not proved.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact Gaussian two-point lower bound and affine upper bound reduce the theorem to the unresolved upper half of the uniform bounded-lift lemma.
open_obligations.attempted: I completed the minimax comparison with the exact modulus and verified the homogeneous diagonal exponent, then traced the remaining rate step to the missing dual transport certificate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Independently of the unresolved rate comparison, the total-modulus rule yields
\[
 \liminf_j\sup_x\mathbb E_x(\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x))^2
 \le\frac54\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2.
\]
For modulus endpoints at radius one, the Gaussian likelihood-ratio calculation gives total variation at most \(\frac12\sqrt{e-1}<1\).  The two-point testing reduction therefore gives
\[
 R^\star\ge\frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8\,
 \omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2.
\]
Thus global minimax risk is proved comparable to the squared exact modulus.  Replacing the modulus by \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), and hence the asserted phase diagram, still requires the missing uniform upper transport inequality isolated for the bounded-lift lemma.  In the homogeneous diagonal calibration, balancing the Holder and standard-error terms gives the stated \(k_0\) and rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The expected-length comparison with the proposed phase envelope is not proved.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact coverage and optimal expected length up to the exact modulus follow, but converting that modulus to the displayed calendar-exhaustion rate requires the unresolved bounded-lift upper inequality.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved exact bias-aware coverage, the affine upper length bound, and the arbitrary-interval two-point lower bound at a covariance-modulus radius.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every \(j\), write \(r=r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), \(b=b_r\), and \(s=s_r>0\).  The exact Gaussian law and total-modulus rule give
\[
 (\widehat\theta_r-\ell(x))/s\sim\mathcal N(t_x,1),\qquad |t_x|\le b/s.
\]
Since \(t\mapsto\Pr\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le c\}\) decreases in \(|t|\), the interval \(C_{\alpha,j}\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly and has the stated factor \(1+j^{-1}\) affine half-length.  If \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), then \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(t)\le t+z_\alpha\), so
\[
 \liminf_j\sup_x\mathbb E_x\operatorname{length}C_{\alpha,j}(Z)
 \le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1).
\]
Conversely, choose \(0<r_\alpha\le1\) with \(\frac12\sqrt{e^{r_\alpha^2}-1}<1-2\alpha\).  The two modulus endpoints and the event that an honest interval contains both imply
\[
 \operatorname{EL}_\alpha^\star
 \ge\left\{1-2\alpha-\tfrac12\sqrt{e^{r_\alpha^2}-1}\right\}
 \omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r_\alpha)
 \gtrsim_\alpha\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1),
\]
where the last inequality follows from concavity.  Thus shortest honest expected length is proved comparable to the exact modulus, and exact coverage is proved.  The advertised comparison with \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) remains contingent on the unresolved bounded-lift upper inequality.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A weakest covariance-aware self-similarity condition and a matching impossibility theorem cannot be formulated from the current handle alone.
open_obligations.obstruction: The adaptation handle is an algorithmic instruction, but the frozen core supplies neither a mathematical self-similarity class nor the multiscale statistics, thresholds, and separation metric needed to quantify honesty and impossibility.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-smoothness modulus proof identifies the correct covariance-whitened scale, but it does not determine a unique weakest self-similarity ordering; inequivalent lower-envelope, polished-tail, and separated-class conditions remain possible.
open_obligations.partial_result: The fixed-smoothness interval is characterized by \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}\).  What remains unspecified is a law-level, covariance-aware self-similarity class and a measurable multiscale statistic defining \(H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\); without those objects there is no well-typed class over which either simultaneous adaptation or its impossibility can be proved.
